name: Motor Assisted Scooter
description: A self-propelled device with handlebars, a deck to stand on or a seat to sit on, an electric motor of not more than 2,000 W, a top speed of 20 mph and the ability to be moved by human power alone; a seated electric two-wheeler too powerful to be an e-bike but held to 20 mph lands here.

restrictions.rule: At least two wheels, working brakes, handlebars, and either a standing deck or a seat to sit, straddle or stand on (Utah Code §41-6a-102)
An electric motor not exceeding 2,000 W and a top speed of 20 mph on a paved level surface, and designed to be propelled by human power alone (Utah Code §41-6a-102)
Not an electric assisted bicycle, moped, motorcycle or motor vehicle (Utah Code §41-6a-102)
Ridden under the rules for bicycles, with no driver's license, registration or insurance (Utah Code §41-6a-1115)

May not be ridden faster than 15 mph, in a public parking structure, where bicycles are prohibited, with more riders than it's designed for, or after being altered from the manufacturer's design (Utah Code §41-6a-1115)
May not be ridden on a freeway (Utah Code §41-6a-1115, as amended by H.B. 381 (2026))
Riders under 21 must wear a helmet meeting 16 CFR part 1203 on a highway, except on one rented from a business
Riders under 8 may not ride with the motor running on public property, a highway, path or sidewalk (Utah Code §41-6a-1115)

Riders 8 to 15 may ride on a highway with the motor running only under a parent's or responsible adult's direct supervision or with a personal electric vehicle safety certificate, and riders 16 and older ride unsupervised (Utah Code §41-6a-1115, as amended by H.B. 381 (2026))
May use a crosswalk, but not negligently or faster than is reasonable (Utah Code §41-6a-1115)
A peace officer who sees a rider under 18 commit a violation may hold the scooter and release it only to a parent or guardian
